newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: FORECAST-UBS sees Q4 Swiss economic decline.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-UBS sees Q4 Swiss economic decline.

text.p: The Swiss economy will continue to decline in the fourth quarter of 1996, and recovery in 1997 depends largely on how briskly exports can grow, Union Bank of Switzerland (UBS) forecast in its latest outlook.

The bank said its quarterly survey of more than 300 industrial companies showed the economy worsened in the third quarter as order inflow, orders on hand and output all dipped from year-earlier levels.
"The business cycle indicator signals declining economic activity for the fourth quarter as well," it said, "but the tempo of the downward trend should not accelerate."
It forecast average 1997 inflation at one percent and said Swiss interest rates would stay low next year, but added fears of unempolyment would keep consumer spending weak.
The hard-pressed construction sector should stabilise only at the end of 1997, but efforts to boost competivieness were supporting the plant and equipment business.
"In light of the dominant domestic economic problems, positive impulses can only come from foreign trade," it said.
"Overall real growth should amount to only around 0.8 percent in 1997 and only in 1998 is it likely to reach it long-term growth potential of 1.5 percent."
UBS pointed out that prices, consumption, wages and output were spiralling lower, but said this was mainly due to one-off factors and increased competitive pressure internationally.
"Although demand is now weak and production is practically stagnant, we do not foresee imminent deflation," it said.
